summary: This is a Snowflake SQL reference page for the DROP CATALOG INTEGRATION command, which removes a catalog integration (an Iceberg catalog integration) from the account. It covers the syntax, the name parameter and its quoting rules, the OWNERSHIP privilege required to run the command, and a usage note that dropped integrations cannot be recovered. Two examples show dropping an integration with and without the IF EXISTS clause. Navigation and boilerplate from the clipped page were ignored.
one_line: Reference for the Snowflake SQL command DROP CATALOG INTEGRATION, which removes a catalog integration, including its syntax, privileges and examples.
key_facts: The DROP CATALOG INTEGRATION command is available to all accounts.
The syntax is DROP CATALOG INTEGRATION [ IF EXISTS ] <name>.
The name parameter specifies the identifier for the catalog integration to drop.
If the identifier contains spaces, special characters, or mixed-case characters, the entire string must be enclosed in double quotes.
Identifiers enclosed in double quotes are case-sensitive, for example "My Catalog".
The role used to execute the command must have the OWNERSHIP privilege on the catalog integration object at a minimum.
OWNERSHIP is a special privilege automatically granted to the role that created the object, and it can be transferred using the role with the MANAGE GRANTS privilege.
Dropped catalog integrations cannot be recovered; they must be recreated.
The example DROP CATALOG INTEGRATION myInt; drops the catalog integration named myInt.
The example DROP CATALOG INTEGRATION IF EXISTS myInt; drops the integration without raising an error if it does not exist.
The page refers to Iceberg catalog integration definitions as the related catalog integration topic.
The page is listed under the Catalog section of the documentation navigation, within the External access and Security areas.
